explanation.headline: FDA's records trace our supply to a plant classified OAI 764 days before the posting

sentences.text: FDA first posted the lidocaine hydrochloride shortage on 2012-02-22 and it remains Current as of 2026-10-21.

An FDA inspection of Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1021343) ended 2010-01-19 and was classified OAI with six observations on control procedures, in-process specifications, and dissemination of problem information.
That OAI inspection occurred 764 days before the shortage posting.
A Warning Letter was issued to Hospira, Inc. on 2010-04-12, 681 days before the posting.
Additional OAI inspections of Hospira, Inc. followed in 2011-06-17 (250 days before posting) and 2011-08-04 (202 days before posting).
Our Corvale East, Corvale General, and Corvale Lakeside sites all hold lidocaine hydrochloride 20 mg/mL 50 mL vials labeled by Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. (NDC 00143-9575-10).

The rule-based best option is to transfer 40 vials of 20 mg/mL 50 mL from Corvale East (18.9 days on hand) to Corvale Lakeside (3.9 days on hand), which would give Lakeside 14 days of supply while East retains two weeks.

memory.text: Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.
